notes: Annual report of the Board of Park Commissioners for the year ending June 30, 1899. Curated: the first of the Chain of Lakes.

coverage.remaining: Not placed or already on the pages: the Spreckels music stand under construction, the railroad depot building cut into five park stations, the '49 Mining Camp cabins kept from the Midwinter Fair, a men's lavatory in Concert Valley, Speed Road sheds, a stone wall on Stanyan Street from Fell to Fulton.

findings.description: The main lake of the new chain at the west end of the park was finished by mid-1899: fifty-five men with an engine and twelve cars had graded the natural hollow down to a foot below the water table, leaving a lake about 1,500 feet long and 100 to 400 feet wide with a winding shore, a creek-like neck of water to the west, and islands planted with birch and rhododendron, alder and fern, willow and iris, and Louisiana swamp cypress.

citation.label: Annual report of the Board of Park Commissioners of San Francisco for the year ending June 30, 1899, New lakes
